sentences.text: Shri Harsh Yadav - Advocate for the appellants.
Shri Manoj Jain - Advocate for respondent no.3.

Order 
This Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellants assailing the impugned award dated 10.11.2025 passed by V Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mandsaur (M.P.) in Claim Case No.103/2024, whereby an amount of Rs.14,57,250/- has been awarded to the appellants, survivors of the deceased Ramsingh Mogiya.
2.
Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the only dispute with regard to the income of the deceased is in the instant appeal.

The Claims Tribunal has taken income as Rs.9,825/- p.m. whereas as per the circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act by the Labour Department of Government of Madhya Pradesh the income of semi skilled labour on the date of incident is Rs.10,682/- as he was engaged in operating well digging machine.

entities.text: Labour Department of Government of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: On this submission prays for enhancement of the award amount.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8673 2 MA-1404-2026 3.

Learned counsel for the Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that the income has been properly assessed by the Claims Tribunal and needs no enhancement and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

4. Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5.

The Apex Court in the case of Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram & Anr. Vs. Mukesh Kumar Yadav reported in (2022) 1 SCC 198 : 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3093 has held that where the income of the deceased is taken on guess work, circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act should be Rupa Bai vs Dulichand on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153343435/
1 resorted to.

entities.text: Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram & Anr. Vs. Mukesh Kumar Yadav reported in (2022) 1 SCC 198 : 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3093
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, on the date of accident i.e. on 24.11.2023 income of the deceased is to be taken as Rs.10,682/- considering him as 'Semi Skilled Labour', whereas the learned Claims Tribunal has taken the income as Rs.9,825/- only.
No other point is under dispute.

Accordingly, the just and proper compensation comes as under:-
Loss of Rs.10,682/- per month + 25% FP less 1/3rd x 12 x 13 Dependency =
Rs.13,88,659/-
 Consortium Rs.1,44,000/-
 Loss of Estate Rs.18,000/-
 Funeral  Rs.18,000/-
 Expenses  Total: Rs.15,68,659/-
 MACT Award: Rs.14,57,250/-
 Enhanced  Rs.1,11,409/-
 Amount 6 .
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.15,68,659/- as against the award of the Trib unal of Rs.14,57,250/-.

Accordingly, the appellants are entitled to an enhanced amount of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:8673 3 MA-1404-2026 Rs.1,11,409/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
7. Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed to the extent indicated herein above.
The other terms and conditions of the impugned award including rate of interest shall remain intact.
(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE RJ Rupa Bai vs Dulichand on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153343435/
